exchanges.body: Any chance you can look at #1493 today? I'd like it merged before the freeze tomorrow at 17:00. Totally get it if the postmortem comes first.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body:
Thanks for waiting, Aisha. The signing itself is right (HMAC-SHA256 over t.body, hex, t= and v1=). The bug is between signing and sending: signature_header signs json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')), but deliver posts json=payload, which requests serializes itself with json.dumps defaults (insertion order, ', ' and ': ' separators). So tenants who verify over the raw request body, as your docs tell them to, will reject every delivery. I checked with a stub requests module: the bytes posted are {"type": "invoice.finalized", "id": "evt_2", ...}, the MAC is over {"data":...,"id":...,"type":...}, and verification fails.

Fix: serialize once to bytes, sign those bytes, post them with data= and Content-Type application/json. The current test can't catch this because it recomputes the MAC the same way the code does; test instead that the signature verifies over the exact bytes deliver() posts (stub requests in sys.modules, no network). Small extra: tell tenants to reject timestamps older than a few minutes, or a captured delivery can be replayed.

exchanges.author: c_aisha
exchanges.subject: Re: #1493
exchanges.body:
Ouch, great catch, thank you. Pushed: signing.prepare(secret, payload, timestamp) serializes once (compact separators) and returns (body bytes, headers); deliver() posts data=body with Content-Type application/json; the test stubs requests and verifies the signature over the exact bytes posted (fails on my first version). Tenant docs now say 'raw request body'.

```diff
+def prepare(secret: str, payload: dict, timestamp: int) -> tuple[bytes, dict]:
+    body = json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
+    mac = hmac.new(secret.encode(), str(timestamp).encode() + b"." + body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
+    return body, {"Content-Type": "application/json", "Tallyfin-Signature": f"t={timestamp},v1={mac}"}
-    with requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers, timeout=timeout, stream=True) as r:
+    data, headers = prepare(secret, payload, int(time.time()))
+    with requests.post(url, data=data, headers=headers, timeout=timeout, stream=True) as r:
```

# Runbook: Celery broker (ElastiCache Redis) failover

Last reviewed: 2026-11-05 (after INC-0412)

finalize_invoice is acks_late: after a broker failover, in-flight tasks are redelivered. Since #1496 (INV-2240) redelivery is safe: side effects are deduplicated on (invoice_id, kind, target).

1. Confirm the failover in the ElastiCache console (events tab) and in #inc channel.
2. Watch the redelivery rate on the billing-worker dashboard; a spike that decays within ~30 minutes is expected.
3. Restart workers only if they're not consuming: `ecs update-service --force-new-deployment` for billing-worker.
4. Never purge the queue: `celery purge` deletes legitimate work (finalizations, reminders) that cannot be recovered.
5. Schedule ElastiCache service updates yourself, off-peak (before 07:00 CT), never leave them to auto-apply.
6. Post in #incidents when the redelivery rate is back to baseline.

# INC-0412 postmortem (draft, blameless). SEV-2, Wednesday 2026-11-04

Summary: an auto-applied ElastiCache service update failed over the Celery broker at 10:04 CT. finalize_invoice (acks_late) tasks were redelivered; side effects weren't deduplicated (INV-2240), so 41 invoices for 9 tenants sent duplicate invoice emails (41) and webhooks (66). Resolved 16:50 after #1496.

Timeline (CT): 10/30 handoff notes the pending update and INV-2240. 11/2 10:00 AWS notice: auto-apply 11/4 10:00-11:00. 11/3 13:45 #1496 opened. 11/4 10:04 failover; 10:05 page; 10:12 SEV-2, Marcus IC; 10:20 queue purge proposed per stale runbook, stopped; 10:31 redeliveries end; 11:15 impact posted; 11:30 hotfix #1497 proposed, not merged (race, locking index); 12:30 #1496 approved as emergency change; 14:52 migration 0042 (107 duplicate rows removed, concurrent unique index); 16:50 resolved.

Impact: 41 duplicate emails, 66 duplicate webhooks (8 tenants with webhooks), downstream duplicate invoices at 2+ tenants' accounting systems. No data loss.

What went wrong: we let the maintenance auto-apply in peak hours; a known idempotency gap (INV-2240) sat as low priority since August; the runbook predated acks_late.
What went right: purge was stopped; the proper fix was already in review; impact numbers were exact within an hour.

Actions: (1) schedule service updates ourselves off-peak (owner Ben, 11/13); (2) runbook rewritten (done 11/5); (3) alert on redelivery spikes (Marcus, 11/20); (4) audit other acks_late tasks for idempotency (Jordan, 12/4); (5) customer-facing summary via CS (Marcus).

documents.title: Support KB: when will a tenant's reminders go out?

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# When will a tenant's reminders go out? (Support KB, Billing, 11/5)

Rule: every payment reminder goes out at 09:00 in the tenant's time zone on its reminder date (3 days before the due date by default).

How to check one:
1. Admin > Tenants > the tenant: the time zone is at the top (e.g. America/Chicago).
2. Reminders tab: 'Remind on' is the local date; 'Send at (UTC)' is when it will go out, in UTC.
3. Convert UTC to the tenant's zone. 09:00 local is 15:00 UTC for Chicago in winter (14:00 in summer), 14:00 UTC for New York in winter, 09:00 UTC for London and Dublin in winter, 16:00 UTC for Phoenix all year (no DST), and 22:00 UTC the previous day for Sydney in its summer (AEDT).
4. The UTC hour moves when clocks change; the local time stays 09:00. That's expected.

As of Thu 11/5 06:04 CT (CHG-3318), every scheduled reminder is at 09:00 local, and new ones are computed correctly (#1494). If a scheduled reminder's Send at doesn't convert to 09:00 local, escalate to Billing on SUP with the tenant and reminder id. Don't edit send times in Admin.
